svg.title: Figure 5-7. Loss scenarios: the driver (C1) (WP-A-05 §5)
svg.desc: Figure 5-7: 6 loss scenario cards for the driver (C1). LS-02 (UCA-04, New finding): The driver corrects with torque below the 100-raw threshold. No override is detected; nothing on screen or in sound changes. Above it, only a grey border. The driver stops correcting, believing the item has yielded. LS-03 (UCA-06, Known gap): The driver has used Experimental Mode, or read upstream docs. The driver expects stops at lights; the reference configuration runs Chill Mode. The driver does not brake for the light or the stopped car. LS-13 (UCA-01, Known gap): The driver engages on a road the item does not handle. Engagement needs only a PCM edge; nothing checks curve radius, road type or glare. The item runs outside what it handles. LS-14 (UCA-02, Known gap): The driver steers against the item and expects that to disengage it. By design steering only overrides; the torque continues as in LS-01. The driver never brakes or cancels. LS-15 (UCA-03, UCA-12, New finding): An EPS temporary fault starts while the driver touches the wheel. No event, or only a silent one; the EPS-fault siren after 1 s is the only cue. The driver reacts late to the silent loss of steering. LS-36 (UCA-07, Known gap): The driver presses the accelerator to pass. The driver sees the grey border and no text, and takes the item to be off. On release the car brakes or accelerates back, unexpected.
svg.text: How each unsafe control action comes about: the cause, what the controller believes or never learns, and the action on the road.
